**Unlocking works again, and Cloak is now portable.** In v0.2.0 and v0.2.1,
a drive unlocked from Cloak started by double-click never actually mounted,
even though the app said "Unlocked". Please update.

## Downloads

| Platform | File | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (x64) | `cloak-v0.2.2-windows-x64.zip` | [WinFsp](https://winfsp.dev) (`winget install WinFsp.WinFsp`) |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `cloak-v0.2.2-macos-arm64.zip` | [macFUSE](https://macfuse.github.io) |

**Windows:** unzip and run `Cloak\Cloak.exe`. Keep the folder together: the
engine is in `Cloak\bin`, and your drive list and settings will be kept in
`Cloak\cloak-data`.

**macOS:** unzip and put `Cloak.app` in a folder you can write to. It isn't
notarized, so clear the download quarantine before first opening it:
`xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine Cloak.app`.

## Fixed

- **Drives didn't mount when Cloak was started by double-click.** With no
  console window, the mount driver failed on its first message and quit
  before the drive appeared. It now runs normally, and the app waits for the
  drive to actually appear: if it doesn't, you see the reason ("The drive
  couldn't be mounted: …") instead of "Unlocked".

## What's new

- **Portable.** Cloak keeps its drive list and settings in a `cloak-data`
  folder next to the app (beside `Cloak.exe`, or beside `Cloak.app`), not
  in your user profile, so it can live on a USB stick. Drives on the same
  stick are still found when it gets a different drive letter on another
  computer. On first run it copies in the drive list and settings from
  earlier versions. If the app's folder can't be written to (Program Files,
  /Applications) it uses `~/.cloak` as before; Settings → Storage shows
  which.
- **The cursor starts in the password box** when you unlock (and in the
  name box for New drive).

## Known limitations

- **The macOS app has not yet been tested on a real Mac.** Treat it as a
  preview and keep a backup of anything you put in a drive.
- Auto-lock runs on sleep, not when the screen locks.
- The app isn't code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run
  (More info → Run anyway).
- FUSE-T is not supported yet (macFUSE only).
- The middle of every file stays plaintext on disk by design.
